Consumer complaint narrative:
I am writing regarding the fraudulent Bank of America account associated with my name. I previously disputed this account and provided a valid police report documenting that the account activity was unauthorized and the result of fraud/identity theft. 
Despite submitting the police report and supporting documentation, Bank of America has failed to remove or block the fraudulent account and has not provided adequate justification for maintaining it. This failure is causing ongoing harm. 
Please be advised that under federal law : 15 U.S.C. 1681c-2 ( FCRA Identity Theft Block ) requires furnishers and credit reporting agencies to block the reporting of information resulting from identity theft once a police report or identity theft report is provided. 
15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ) requires furnishers, including banks, to conduct a reasonable investigation and correct or delete inaccurate or fraudulent information after receiving a dispute.

15 U.S.C. 1693 et seq. ( Electronic Fund Transfer Act ) and 12 C.F.R. 1005 ( Regulation E ) require financial institutions to investigate unauthorized transactions and limit consumer liability for fraud. 
I have complied with my obligations by promptly disputing the account and providing a police report. Bank of Americas continued failure to remove or properly resolve this fraudulent account may constitute violations of the Fair Credit Reporting Act and the Electronic Fund Transfer Act. 
I am requesting the following : Immediate removal and closure of the fraudulent account Written confirmation of the results of your investigation Correction of any reporting related to this account If this matter is not resolved promptly, I am prepared to pursue further regulatory and legal remedies, including escalation to the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency and additional action under applicable federal law. 
Please respond in writing.

Consumer complaint narrative:
On XX/XX/XXXX, I purchased a XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX : XXXX ) from XXXX XXXX XXXX for {$16000.00}, with a {$4000.00} down payment. The loan was originated with XXXX XXXX ( Account : XXXX ). The sale and financing were procured through fraudulent acts by the dealership. I would like to also highlight that I am a visibly XXXX man, who has just lost two cars in XXXX XXXX. 

Fraudulent Inducement : The manager, XXXX XXXX, explicitly told me the loan could be refinanced after a period of timely payments. This statement was a material misrepresentation that induced me to agree to the loan terms. I later confirmed with the lender that no such refinancing option exists.

Defective Vehicle & Warranty Fraud : The dealership knowingly sold me a vehicle with serious, latent defects. They failed to honor written concessions to replace unsafe tires and a defective radio. A concerning noise reported in XX/XX/XXXX was diagnosed in XX/XX/XXXX and repaired in XX/XX/XXXX as a failed CV axle. I later discovered from a XXXX dealer in XX/XX/XXXX that the vehicle had a pre-existing defect in its exhaust manifold that needed complete replacement. A repair at XXXX XXXX in XX/XX/XXXX revealed a hose had been duct-taped since before purchase, causing a coolant/airflow hose repair costing over {$600.00}. In XX/XX/XXXX, the engine catastrophically failedapproximately 30 months post-purchase and within the same year the warranty expiredrequiring an {$8200.00} repair. The car is now inoperable and worthless. 

Undisclosed GAP Insurance : I subsequently discovered the dealership added a charge for GAP insurance to my contract without my knowledge or consent. This product was never discussed, disclosed, or agreed upon.

Fraud Confirmed : The fraud was further confirmed when I was required to re-sign the Bill of Sale under new management with a new date of XX/XX/XXXX, while other documents were not re-signed. The dealership is now permanently closed. 

Financial Harm : I am left with a loan payoff balance exceeding {$14000.00} ( see attached payoff quote ) for a destroyed vehicle. Repair costs total beyond {$8200.00}. The dealership 's fraud directly caused this financial loss. 

Lender Liability : Under the FTC Holder Rule ( 16 C.F.R. Part 433 ), the lender is liable for this dealer fraud. I have made formal demand to the lender for loan rescission. They continue reporting the debt as delinquent without noting it is disputed, in violation of the FCRA.
